newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity trades mixed, COB follows natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity trades mixed, COB follows natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed Thursday, with February California Oregon Border (COB) following natural gas futures lower, industry sources said.

As of 1210 EST, February COB lost 24 cents to $13.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) after morning exchanges as high as $13.60, while March COB was steady at $11.65 after changing hands as high as $11.70 per MWh.
February Palo Verde traded steady at $15.65 per MWh, while March PV was bid at $13.50 and offered at $13.80 from Wednesday's settle at $13.80 per MWh.
April PV had traded at a new contract low of $12.95 per MWh.
As of 1225 EST, NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 13.3 cents at $2.775 per million British thermal units, under pressure from forecasts of mild weather next week.
Forecasts showed the U.S. Northwest would experience slightly below-normal temperatures through the weekend with chances of coastal rain and mountain snow.
Meanwhile, the Southwest would enjoy a warming trend through the weekend with above-normal precipitation for California and the Great Basin with below normal precipitation in the desert Southwest.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 15 COB contracts had traded as of 1025 EST, while a PV volume estimate was not available.
COB open interest for Jan 22 fell 138 to 3,258 while PV open interest fell 33 to 1,375, NYMEX said.
